headline: KOSPI's 5.2% 'Black Friday' on new US chip-export curbs sends money into KTBs: the 10Y falls 8.5bp to 3.857% and the 3Y 7.4bp to 3.642%, with only about 1.4bp of the 10Y move explained by Treasuries
summary: KTBs had their biggest rally in a month as KOSPI fell 5.21% to 4,869.96 with sell sidecars triggered on both boards: the 3Y fell 7.4bp to 3.642% (49th percentile of its 1-year range), the 10Y 8.5bp to 3.857% (43rd) and the 30Y only 3.1bp to 4.000%, so the 5–10Y belly led and the long end lagged (10s30s steepened 5.4bp to 14.3bp). Over the week the 3Y is down 11.7bp and the 10Y 14.4bp. The 1Y slipped just 1.6bp to 3.620% (88th) and bills held near 1-year highs (MSB 91-day 3.198%, CD up 1bp to 3.39%, CP 3.84%), so a November 26 hike is still priced and 1s2s collapsed to 3.5bp, a 1-year low. MSB 2Y fell 4.4bp to 3.696%, now 4.1bp over KTB. Spread products lagged except KDB: the refitted KDB 3Y (28 trades) tightened 9.5bp to 13.2bp over KTB (20th), while AAA bank 1Y widened to 42.0bp (92nd), AA- 3Y to 68.7bp (79th) and KEPCO 3Y to 41.3bp (83rd).
drivers: KOSPI fell 267.93 points (5.21%) to 4,869.96, a 10-month low, after the Nasdaq lost 2.25% and new US rules forced Samsung and TSMC to pause some chip shipments to China; Samsung fell 7.0% and foreigners sold about KRW 1.27tn of stocks for a sixth day. Bonds took the other side all day: the 3Y moved back below 3.70% for the first time in ten sessions.
Foreign 3Y futures buying, contracts still cheap

Foreigners turned from early sellers to buyers of 12,541 3Y futures (only 256 10Y), extending a seven-week run of net futures buying even as WGBI index buying has ended and they turned net sellers of cash KTBs this month. The KRX 3Y settled 24 ticks higher at 103.79 and the 10Y 73 ticks higher at 109.43, its biggest gain in a month. Our basket fair values are 103.85 and 109.41, so the 3Y still trades about 6 ticks cheap (9 yesterday) and the 10Y about 2 ticks rich.

The US 10Y fell 3bp to 5.04% (par yield) as the S&P 500 lost 2.0% for a sixth day, the Philly Fed index dropped to 6.3 (f 20.0) and continuing claims jumped, although prices paid rose to 58.2. At the 1-year beta of 0.48 that implied −1.4bp for the KTB 10Y; it fell 8.5bp, so about 7.1bp was local. The KTB–UST 10Y gap widened to −118.3bp, the widest of the past year (0th percentile).

Bills and the 1Y barely moved: brokers (SC, Hana, Deutsche) all expect a hike to 3.25% on Nov 26, with Deutsche seeing 3.75% by Q2 2027 and Hana a 3.50% dot-plot median. October PPI fell 0.1% m/m (+7.2% y/y, down from 7.6%) on cheaper farm goods, a small help. USD/KRW rose 6.2 won to 1,336.2, which capped the rally in the afternoon.
data: Mildly dovish; farm prices, not core.
Almost all saw further hikes as likely appropriate
view: Today was overwhelmingly local: Treasuries implied −1.4bp for the 10Y and it fell 8.5bp, and over four weeks the 10Y's −24bp splits into +5.2bp from Treasuries (weekly beta 0.65, US 10Y +8bp) and −29.2bp of Korea's own rally, so this is a domestic risk-off trade, not imported duration.

The rotation signal still reads bond rally and firmed slightly (weekly +1.34, daily +1.40) as KOSPI's four-week loss deepened to 12.3%, margin credit sits 13.5% lower and broker deposits are down KRW 8.3tn.

But the BOK is still set to hike on Nov 26 and 1s2s is only 3.5bp, so the curve has little room left to price cuts; I expect the 10Y to trade 3.78–3.95% into the meeting and keep the belly rich (3s5s10s −4.3bp, 10th percentile) rather than chase it.

Book: the 10Y long reached within 0.7bp of its 3.85% target, so take half off (+11.8bp outright, about +12bp hedged) and trail the rest; the KDB 3Y overweight hit its 18bp target (+11.7bp) on a refit with 28 trades and is closed.

Hold the remaining rally view against Treasuries rather than outright: hedged rally calls were right 68% of the time and sell-off calls 69% (Sharpe 1.38, worst drawdown −26bp) against 52%, 57%, 0.97 and −36bp outright; a hawkish dot plot or a KOSPI rebound above 5,300 are the main risks.

buckets.name: KTB 1–2Y front end
buckets.why: The 2Y fell 6.7bp to 3.655%, 63rd percentile of its 1-year range (average 3.40%), while the 1Y slipped only 1.6bp to 3.620% (88th), so 1s2s collapsed 5.1bp to 3.5bp, a 1-year low (average 29.6bp), and 2s3s is −1.3bp (0th). MSB 91-day (3.198%) and CD (3.39%, a 1-year high) still price a hike to 3.25% on Nov 26.
buckets.call: Keep: buy the 2Y above 3.80%, target 3.65%, stop 3.90%. Not triggered (14.5bp away).

buckets.name: 3s10s curve
buckets.why: 3s10s flattened another 1.1bp to 21.5bp (0th percentile, average 39.4bp, 1-year low 20.8bp) as the 5–10Y led the rally. The 3s5s10s fly is −4.3bp (10th, average 4.2bp), so the belly is rich. Our earlier steepener was stopped on Nov 5.
buckets.call: Stay flat: KOSPI closed at 4,870, far below the 5,300 re-entry trigger. Re-enter the steepener (3 × 3Y vs 1 × 10Y futures, DV01 about KRW 87k each side) only on a KOSPI close above 5,300 or after the BOK hike; target 32bp, stop 19bp.

buckets.name: KTB 10Y outright
buckets.why: The 10Y at 3.857% sits at the 43rd percentile of a 3.25–4.60% range (average 3.92%), down 14.4bp this week. Treasuries implied −1.4bp and the 10Y fell 8.5bp, so the hedged long gained about 7bp today. On Thursday's trades the new 10Y (26-13) was the richest liquid line (about 4bp through the curve); 25-3 and 26-3 in the 3–4Y area were the cheapest (+4–5bp).
buckets.call: Adjust: target 3.85% missed by 0.7bp; take half profit at 3.857% (+11.8bp outright, about +12bp hedged). Hold the rest against about 0.5 × US 10Y, new target 3.78%, stop raised to 3.93%.

buckets.name: Ultra-long 30–50Y
buckets.why: 30s50s held at −2.4bp as the 30Y and 50Y both fell 3.1bp, still at the 86th percentile (average −9.0bp), so the 50Y stays cheap against history. The long end lagged the rally: 10s30s steepened 5.4bp to 14.3bp (76th) and the 10s20s30s fly rose 4.4bp to 19.1bp (91st), with the 20Y the cheapest point.
buckets.call: Flat after Tuesday's +5.6bp target. Re-enter the 30Y-into-50Y switch on a back-up to 0bp; target −5bp, stop +2.5bp. Not triggered.

buckets.name: KDB 1–3Y vs KTB
buckets.why: The KDB curve was refitted on 28 trades and now puts the 3Y 13.2bp over KTB, 9.5bp tighter and at the 20th percentile (average 19.6bp), which hit our 18bp target; part of the move is the refit, so treat the level with care. The 1Y fit is 29.4bp over (67th) against 23.4bp for KOFIA's 1Y quote (42nd). IBK 1Y is 32.4bp over on 15 trades (77th); KEXIM is 24.8bp flat across tenors on only 4 trades, low confidence.
buckets.call: Closed: overweight KDB 3Y from 24.9bp hit the 18bp target, +11.7bp. Re-enter above 22bp; meanwhile prefer KDB 1Y over KTB 1Y if adding policy-bank paper.

buckets.name: AAA bank debentures and money market
buckets.why: On 34 trades the bank fit puts the 1Y 42.0bp over KTB, 2.5bp wider and at the 92nd percentile (average 31.0bp), as banks did not follow the KTB rally; the 3Y is 28.4bp over (49th). CD rose 1bp to 3.39%, a 1-year high, and CP held at 3.84%, so CP–CD is 45bp (88th, average 29bp) and CD–MSB91 19bp (35th).
buckets.call: No change: revisit bank paper once CP–CD falls below 35bp; prefer the 1Y over the 3Y if adding.

buckets.name: Corporate credit (AA- 3Y)
buckets.why: AA- 3Y fell 6.1bp to 4.329% but lagged the KTB 3Y, so the spread widened 1.3bp to 68.7bp (79th percentile, average 61.6bp). KEPCO 3Y is 41.3bp over (83rd, average 34.8bp) and BBB- minus AA- 583bp (79th). Credit is drifting wider as equities crack.
buckets.call: Add AA- only above 75bp or once KOSPI regains 5,300; no trigger hit.

watch: Next: US S&P Global PMIs (Nov 20 US time), Korea Nov 1–20 exports (Nov 21), US jobless claims (Nov 25), the BOK decision, dot plot and new forecasts plus the MOEF December issuance plan on Nov 26 (hike to 3.25% priced), and the FOMC on Dec 8–9; KTBs take about 0.48bp per Treasury bp on the day, but local risk-off is driving them now.
